items.title: New York court lets a sexual-assault-related negligence claim escape a sorority arbitration clause
items.publisher: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Second Department
items.summary: The court held that the Ending Forced Arbitration of Sexual Assault and Sexual Harassment Act can prevent arbitration of a negligence claim against a party that did not commit the alleged assault. A student alleges her sorority required attendance at a fraternity event and failed to protect members there. Because that claim has a logical connection to the alleged assault, the court treated it as a case that ‘relates to’ a sexual-assault dispute under the federal statute.

items.title: Freeport school district has only a revocable right to use village parkland
items.publisher: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Second Department
items.summary: The court affirmed that the Village of Freeport owns disputed parkland free of any property interest held by the local school district; the district has only an easement in gross or revocable license to use it. An easement appurtenant would alienate parkland and therefore required direct, specific legislative authorization, which the district could not show. The decision applies New York’s public-trust doctrine to a long-running arrangement between two public bodies.

items.title: Failure to file a six-month town claim defeats a union contract suit despite an arbitral win
items.publisher: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Second Department
items.summary: The court affirmed dismissal of a union and employee’s contract action against Eastchester because they had not filed the verified claim required by Town Law § 65(3) within six months. The union had prevailed in nonbinding arbitration over a promotion governed by seniority, but the town rejected the award. Because the later suit sought damages as well as equitable relief and alleged no continuing violation, the statutory filing condition could not be excused.

items.title: CMS immediately pauses new federal-exchange broker registrations through February 2027
items.summary: An interim final rule authorizes and immediately imposes a moratorium on Plan Year 2027 registration for agents and brokers who lack a current 2026 agreement with the federally facilitated health-insurance exchanges. The pause runs until February 1, 2027, unless changed earlier, and does not cover state-run exchanges. CMS invokes the Administrative Procedure Act’s good-cause exception and says the interval will be used to add safeguards against unauthorized enrollment, misuse of personal data, and related misconduct.

items.title: Workers with nondegree credentials report 16.4% higher median earnings
items.summary: Combined 2019–2024 Survey of Income and Program Participation data show full-time workers ages 25–64 with a certificate, certification, or license reported median annual earnings 16.4% above otherwise grouped workers without one. The association was strongest among people with less formal education: high-school graduates with both a certificate and certification or license earned about 21% more. Census cautions that the survey cannot establish causation because it does not record when credentials were earned or whether they match current jobs.

items.title: Commerce creates a company-by-company route to pharmaceutical tariff relief
items.publisher: U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security
items.summary: Commerce issued procedures for importers to seek tariff adjustments for patented pharmaceuticals and ingredients that meet an urgent U.S. health need. Eligible categories include orphan, fertility, nuclear-medicine, cell- and gene-therapy products; applications must document patients, alternatives, origin, and manufacturers. The notice also lists eligible trading jurisdictions and creates a zero-duty heading for covered products imported solely for clinical trials, research, or other noncommercial uses. Decisions will be company- and product-specific after interagency consultation.

items.title: HUD will auction about $1.3 billion in reverse mortgages on vacant homes
items.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
items.summary: HUD announced an October 27 competitive sale of roughly 4,200 due-and-payable reverse mortgages with an aggregate balance near $1.3 billion. The first liens cover vacant single-family properties whose borrowers are deceased and have no surviving nonborrowing spouse; the loans will be sold without Federal Housing Administration insurance and with servicing released. HUD describes the seventeenth such offering as a way to reduce Mutual Mortgage Insurance Fund risk and dispose of defaulted assets efficiently.

items.title: Coinbase Derivatives files rules for cash-settled and perpetual single-stock futures
items.publisher: Coinbase Derivatives, LLC / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
items.summary: Coinbase Derivatives filed an immediately effective rule change governing cash-settled futures on individual stocks and exchange-traded funds, including perpetual single-stock futures. Initial listings would be limited to especially liquid securities: generally at least $100 billion in market capitalization, more than 20 million shares of estimated deliverable supply, and $450 million in average daily transaction value over six months. The filing establishes exchange rules and eligibility thresholds; it is not evidence that any particular contract has begun trading.

items.title: Access Board revises FOIA deadlines, search fees, and accessibility procedures
items.summary: The Access Board’s final Freedom of Information Act rule now states the ordinary 20-working-day response deadline, tolls that clock while clarification is sought, and permits denial when a request remains insufficiently described. Its fee schedule adds information-technology searches at a GS-13-equivalent rate and ties categories to current federal pay scales. The Board declined to promise accessible records automatically in every format, instead pointing to disability-specific accommodations under section 504 and accessible agency communications under section 508.

items.title: Presidential proclamation extends the $100,000 condition on certain H-1B entries for one year
items.summary: Proclamation 11069 extends through September 21, 2027, the prior restriction on entry of certain H-1B workers unless the supporting petition is accompanied or supplemented by a $100,000 payment, subject to limited exceptions. The document reports that payment has been made for more than 700 petitions since the restriction began in 2025. Its claims that outsourcing firms suppress wages and displace U.S. workers are the administration’s stated rationale, not independent findings established by the proclamation itself.

items.title: NHTSA lets states use different 2027 safety targets in two federal programs
items.summary: NHTSA waived, for fiscal 2027, its rule requiring states to submit identical performance targets in highway-safety plans and Federal Highway Administration improvement-program reports. The two programs operate under different statutes: NHTSA targets must show constant or improved performance, while the highway program lacks that constraint and is undergoing a separate rulemaking. The agency made the waiver effective immediately without notice and comment, citing incompatible deadlines and the need to give states flexibility while the other rulemaking proceeds.

items.title: DEA proposes Schedule I controls for five synthetic tryptamine hallucinogens
items.summary: DEA proposes placing 4-OH-DiPT, 5-MeO-AMT, 5-MeO-MiPT, 5-MeO-DET, and DiPT in Schedule I, which would extend criminal and administrative controls to manufacture, possession, research, and other handling. The agency says all five have appeared in seizures and abuse reports, lack accepted U.S. medical uses, and were recommended for Schedule I by Health and Human Services evaluations delivered in 2012. Those are agency assessments supporting a proposed rule; comments and hearing requests remain open through October 23.

items.title: NIH offers a targeted stem-cell-transplant conditioning technology for licensing
items.summary: NIH made patent rights available for a recombinant minibody-toxin designed to deplete hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells before transplantation by targeting the cMPL receptor. Conventional conditioning relies on cytotoxic chemotherapy or radiation that can cause substantial morbidity and exclude older or medically fragile patients. NIH identifies a short half-life, marrow penetration, and reduced chemotherapy toxicity as potential advantages, but the technology remains preclinical and the notice reports only animal in-vivo data rather than demonstrated safety or efficacy in people.

items.title: South Atlantic red-snapper recreational season is limited to three days
items.summary: NOAA set the 2026 South Atlantic recreational red-snapper season from October 9 through October 11, closing at 12:01 a.m. on October 12. The fishery’s annual recreational limit is 22,797 fish, and anglers may retain one per person per day without a size limit. The season’s length functions as the accountability measure intended to give anglers access while constraining total harvest; the notice announces the dates rather than presenting a new stock assessment.

items.title: FDA panel examines a blood test intended to screen for multiple cancers
items.summary: FDA’s Molecular and Clinical Genetics Panel met to consider GRAIL’s premarket-approval application for Galleri, a prescription blood test intended to detect cancer-specific methylation patterns in cell-free DNA in adults 50 and older and predict the likely tissue of origin. The agency posted executive summaries, panel questions, and voting questions. The advisory committee’s recommendations are nonbinding, and the posted page does not itself report an FDA approval decision; positive signals would still require diagnostic follow-up.
